boards.school_name: The University of Texas at Austin
boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented UT Austin traditions spanning campus ceremonies, school songs, spirit symbols, and football-pageantry objects.

cards.title: Hook ’em Horns
cards.subtitle: UT Austin spirit hand sign
cards.notes: Use the hand sign at an approved campus or athletics event; the university traces its first demonstration to a 1955 Gregory Gym pep rally.
cards.short_summary: A hand signal introduced by head cheerleader Harley Clark in 1955 and adopted as UT’s official sign.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Athletics says Harley Clark created the Hook ’em Horns hand sign in 1955 and it was adopted as the University’s official hand sign.
cards.access_notes: Participate only where event staff and venue policies permit.

cards.title: Sing “The Eyes of Texas”
cards.subtitle: UT Austin school song
cards.notes: Listen for the school song at the end of a University ceremony or sporting event, then follow the program’s participation guidance.
cards.short_summary: UT’s 1903 school song remains part of the close of sporting events and University ceremonies.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin states that “The Eyes of Texas” was written and first performed by students in 1903 and is sung at the end of sporting events and University ceremonies.
cards.access_notes: Follow current event guidance for participation.

cards.title: Join the “Texas Fight!” Yell
cards.subtitle: UT Austin fight song
cards.notes: At a game or spirit event, follow the band or emcee for the familiar yell section instead of trying to cue it yourself.
cards.short_summary: The fight song debuted at the 1923 Texas–Texas A&M football game and incorporates “The Eyes of Texas.”
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin identifies “Texas Fight!” as first performed at the 1923 football game against Texas A&M and notes that it quotes “The Eyes of Texas.”
cards.access_notes: Participate through official game or campus programming.

cards.title: Read the Tower’s Orange Signal
cards.subtitle: Main Building Tower lighting tradition
cards.notes: View the Tower from public campus space after dark and use UT’s lighting guide to understand the orange and special configurations.
cards.short_summary: Since 1937, Tower lighting has marked University milestones and academic or athletic achievements.
cards.evidence_claim: UT’s Tower office states that the Tower has been lit since 1937 to celebrate Longhorn accomplishments and University milestones.
cards.access_notes: Observe from publicly accessible campus areas; Tower access is not required.

cards.title: Start at Gone to Texas
cards.subtitle: Incoming-student welcome celebration
cards.notes: If you are an incoming student, check orientation communications for the official event details held on the eve of the first class day.
cards.short_summary: A Tower-front celebration that UT describes as the official start of Longhorn life for incoming students.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin says thousands of incoming students gather before the Tower on the eve of their first day of class for Gone to Texas, marking the official start of Longhorn life.
cards.access_notes: Designed for incoming students; confirm the current schedule through official new-student communications.

cards.title: Spot Big Bertha
cards.subtitle: Longhorn Band bass drum tradition
cards.notes: Look for the enormous bass drum during a football performance, or see its stated permanent home in the stadium’s north end-zone concourse.
cards.short_summary: The Longhorn Band’s eight-foot drum has been a focal point since 1955.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Athletics states that Big Bertha has been a Longhorn Band focal point since 1955 and is escorted at football games by the Bertha Crew.
cards.access_notes: Stadium-concourse access depends on the event and venue entry rules.

cards.title: Hear Smokey at Football
cards.subtitle: Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium
cards.notes: At a Texas football game, expect the cannon from the stadium’s southeast corner after Texas scores and at quarter breaks; protect sensitive ears.
cards.short_summary: A student-operated replica cannon fired as part of Texas Football’s game-day sequence.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Athletics identifies Smokey as a Texas Football gameday element, fired after Texas scores and at end-of-quarter breaks.
cards.access_notes: The cannon is loud; follow stadium staff instructions and consider hearing protection.

cards.title: Learn the Red-Candle Hex Rally
cards.subtitle: Main Mall rivalry-week tradition
cards.notes: When officially scheduled, attend the campus rally and follow organizers’ directions; its modern version revived a 1941 red-candle ritual.
cards.short_summary: A Texas Exes Student Chapter-era rally built around a revived red-candle ritual before the Texas–Texas A&M game.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin documents the 1941 red-candle hex and says the first modern Texas Hex Rally occurred on Main Mall in 1986.
cards.access_notes: Only participate through an officially scheduled event; do not use open flames outside permitted programming.

cards.title: See Bevo’s Game-Day Appearance
cards.subtitle: UT Austin live Longhorn mascot
cards.notes: At an official Texas Athletics appearance, view Bevo from designated spectator areas and give the handlers and animal ample space.
cards.short_summary: The live Longhorn mascot tradition began with Bevo’s first public football-game appearance in 1916.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Athletics states that Bevo first appeared at a UT football game on Nov. 30, 1916 and that the legacy continues through successive Bevos.
cards.access_notes: Observe only from designated areas and follow all handler and event instructions.

cards.title: End Commencement with Tower Fireworks
cards.subtitle: Spring Commencement finale
cards.notes: For a commencement ceremony you are eligible to attend, remain through the finale and follow event staff directions for viewing areas.
cards.short_summary: UT made fireworks the standard finale to its spring Commencement ceremony in 1994.
cards.evidence_claim: UT Austin’s Commencement office says fireworks were introduced as a standard finale to the ceremony in 1994.
cards.access_notes: Occurs as part of official commencement programming; follow current attendance and safety guidance.
